strategies.entry_summary: Trade in the direction of the session idea after price extends away from VWAP to at least the first, preferably the second, standard-deviation band, then breaks back and retests that level before resuming. strategies.exit_summary: Use the second or third standard-deviation bands as profit targets. No explicit stop-loss rule is taught, but the target/management mechanic is stated as exiting at outer VWAP bands.

strategies.name: vwap_mean_reversion_from_outer_bands
strategies.entry_summary: Use outer VWAP standard-deviation bands as overbought/oversold extremes for reversal trades, entering when price reaches the extreme bands and looking for rebalancing back toward fair value. The setup is framed as using those bands as the most convenient premium/discount price of the session.
strategies.exit_summary: Target the central VWAP as the price-rebalancing objective. The speaker explicitly says to use central VWAP as the target for reversal trades.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: use first/second/third standard-deviation bands as overbought or oversold contextual levels
variants.transcript_quote: if you're using reversal strategies you might want to use these as some sort of overbought or oversold levels... and use the central vwap as a target

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches two opposing executable VWAP skeletons: trend-continuation after a break/retest versus mean-reversion from outer deviation bands back to VWAP. A stop-loss rule is not clearly taught for either, so exits are limited to the stated target mechanics.
